To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gap‐junctional communication is reduced and altered in human primary liver tumors, and that the reduction is due to the lack of functional gap junctions rather than to the lack of connexin proteins.

(1) gap‐junctional communication (GJ) is reduced in primary human liver tumor tissues, (2) GJ is selectively reduced between tumor and non‐tumoral cells, and (3) connexin (Cx) 32 is aberrantly localized in tumor cells.

the major liver gap junction protein, connex 32, is aberrantly localized in primary human liver tumor cells, probably due to disruption of its normal targeting mechanisms, but is not structurally altered, and that this abnormality is associated with a significant reduction of gap‐junctional cell‐to‐cell communication capacity in liver tumors.
